data.name: Rose and Lotus: Petals of Memories
data.detailed_description:
I'm definitely going to escape from this house...!

[Rose and Lotus: Petals of Memories] is based on Korean traditional fairy tales 'Janghwa, Hongryeon'.
The main character, Janghwa, awake from the cold floor without her memory.
Find the truth behind the dark mansion and get out of it with your sister Hongryeon.




Key Features:
  • Point-and-Click Adventure in the Dark Mansion
  • A reinterpretation of traditional fairy tales
  • Unique artwork that varies from room to room
  • A well-organized configuration of various puzzles.
  • beautiful background music


How to play:
[Rose and Lotus: Petals of Memories] is a point-and-click game.
Observation and only the mouse are needed.
Click on the placed object -> Zoom in to find hidden clues
You must enter the correct answer for the puzzle or apply the item to the correct location.




Mission:
Rooms are connected to each other.
There are three to four puzzles in each room, and if you solve all the puzzles that make up the area, you will be given a clue to move to the next room.
The goal is to advance the room, reach the final destination, and leave the house.




Story:
Each section has an iconic story.
Cut-scene animation and simple conversation events tell you stories hidden in your home one by one.
When you solve the puzzle, you can you can approach the storyline naturally.





📢 Guidelines for Game Video and Streaming Broadcasts:
To prevent spoilers, game video and streaming broadcasts are allowed only up to [Chapter6: Engrave].
We kindly request your cooperation to accommodate a larger audience of gamers.
Thank you.

reviews.review:
Rose and Lotus: Petals of Memories is a distinctive puzzle adventure that combines Korean folklore, mystery, and escape-room gameplay into a surprisingly engaging experience. Developed by 5minlab Corp. and published by 5minlab Corp. together with KRAFTON, Inc., the game draws inspiration from the classic tale of Janghwa and Hongryeon, transforming a familiar legend into a haunting journey through a mysterious mansion filled with secrets. Rather than relying on fast-paced action or horror clichés, the game focuses on exploration, puzzle-solving, and gradual storytelling, creating an experience that feels thoughtful and immersive from beginning to end.

The story begins with Janghwa awakening inside an unfamiliar mansion with little understanding of how she arrived there. Accompanied by her sister Hongryeon, she must search the mansion for clues while attempting to recover lost memories and uncover the truth hidden within its walls. This setup immediately establishes an atmosphere of uncertainty and intrigue. The narrative unfolds slowly through environmental storytelling, notes, symbolic imagery, and discoveries made during exploration. Instead of delivering answers immediately, the game encourages players to piece together events themselves, making the mystery more rewarding as new revelations emerge.

One of the game's greatest strengths is its approach to puzzles. Every room feels carefully designed to challenge observation and logical thinking. Players must inspect objects, search for clues, decipher patterns, and connect information scattered throughout the environment. The puzzles are varied enough to remain interesting throughout the adventure, avoiding the repetitive feeling that often affects games in the genre. Solving a difficult puzzle provides a genuine sense of accomplishment because progress usually comes from paying attention to details rather than relying on trial and error.

The mansion itself serves as one of the game's most memorable features. Each area possesses a unique visual identity, with different themes, decorative styles, and unsettling details that constantly encourage curiosity. Exploring new rooms never loses its appeal because there is always the possibility of discovering another cleverly designed puzzle or narrative clue. The environments are not only visually attractive but also meaningful to the story, reinforcing the emotional and psychological themes that run throughout the adventure.

Atmosphere plays a crucial role in the overall experience. Rose and Lotus: Petals of Memories excels at creating tension without overusing jump scares or aggressive horror elements. Instead, it builds unease through its lonely setting, eerie visual design, and mysterious storyline. The mansion often feels as though it exists somewhere between reality and memory, a place shaped by forgotten experiences and unresolved emotions. This subtle approach to horror makes the game more captivating because players remain invested in uncovering the truth rather than simply anticipating the next scare.

The artistic presentation deserves special praise. The game's visual style effectively balances beauty and darkness, reflecting the fairy-tale origins of its story while maintaining an unsettling tone. Character portraits, environmental details, and symbolic imagery all contribute to a dreamlike atmosphere that helps distinguish the game from many other indie puzzle adventures. The developers clearly invested considerable effort into making each location memorable, and that attention to detail significantly enhances the overall immersion.

The soundtrack complements the experience effectively. Rather than dominating the experience, the music quietly supports the emotional tone of each scene. Soft melodies and atmospheric tracks strengthen moments of mystery, sadness, and suspense while allowing players to focus on exploration and puzzle-solving. Combined with ambient sound effects, the audio design helps create a consistently immersive environment that supports the narrative themes of memory, loss, and discovery.

Gameplay remains accessible thanks to simple controls and an intuitive interface. Interacting with objects, examining clues, and navigating between rooms feels straightforward, making the game easy to approach even for players who are not experienced with adventure games. This simplicity allows the focus to remain on the puzzles and story. However, players seeking action-heavy gameplay or complex combat systems may find the experience too slow-paced, as the game is firmly dedicated to its puzzle-adventure roots.

The pacing can occasionally become challenging, particularly when players encounter a difficult puzzle that interrupts narrative progression. Some solutions require careful observation and patience, which may frustrate those looking for a more relaxed experience. Nevertheless, these moments generally feel fair because the clues are usually present within the environment. For dedicated puzzle fans, these challenges are likely to be among the most enjoyable parts of the game.

What ultimately makes Rose and Lotus: Petals of Memories stand out is its successful fusion of traditional folklore and modern puzzle design. By using the legendary story of Janghwa and Hongryeon as a foundation, the game achieves a unique identity that separates it from more generic mystery adventures. Its combination of engaging puzzles, strong atmosphere, memorable visual design, and intriguing storytelling results in an experience that feels both culturally distinctive and universally appealing.

For players who enjoy escape-room mechanics, narrative-driven exploration, and atmospheric mysteries, Rose and Lotus: Petals of Memories offers a rewarding journey filled with clever challenges and emotional storytelling. While its deliberate pacing and puzzle-focused structure may not appeal to everyone, those willing to immerse themselves in its world will discover a carefully crafted adventure that lingers in the mind long after the final puzzle has been solved.

Rating: 7/10
